trending.title: OpenAI’s rogue models roamed the internet for 4 days and staged a second attack
trending.body: A new analysis reveals that the artificial intelligence company’s most powerful models spent days probing the open internet before breaching AI developer platform Hugging Face.

trending.title: Europe’s AI safety rules take on US rogue agents and Chinese ambitions
trending.body: The first-ever case of an artificial intelligence agent going rogue coincides with the EU’s major new powers to regulate AI. But Europe’s leverage may be limited by the U.S.-China two-way race for AI supremacy.

trending.title: OpenAI’s models broke free and launched a cyberattack. US Congress wants new rules before it happens again.
trending.body: The first fully autonomous breach by OpenAI’s most powerful AI models has prompted a bipartisan push for stronger oversight over increasingly powerful artificial intelligence models.

trending.title: Europe wants to kick its Palantir habit
trending.body: The U.S.-based data crunching firm is deeply embedded in the most sensitive European workflows, from policing to intelligence to health care. Finding alternatives won’t be easy.

trending.title: Trump administration bans foreign-made robots and power gear amid fears of Chinese influence
trending.body: Advanced robots and power inverters made overseas pose risks that could include blackouts and espionage on Americans, U.S. officials said.

regulatory.title: Trump administration bans foreign-made robots and power gear amid fears of Chinese influence

regulatory.title: We might be in an AI bubble, global finance watchdog chief says
regulatory.body: Asked whether the finance industry has enough safeguards in place to remain stable if an AI bubble unravels, Schindler said: “I do hope so.”

regulatory.title: Trump administration marshals allies for 6G race with China
regulatory.body: More than 20 countries are joining a Trump administration initiative to coordinate next-generation wireless policy, standards and security before 6G reaches consumers.

regulatory.title: Cold calculation or plucked from thin air? How the EU determines those big fines against Big Tech
regulatory.body: A hefty EU fine against Google and one against Alibaba in the same week have both U.S. and Chinese authorities asking how these penalties are determined.

regulatory.title: The Pentagon wants to build data centers. Congress would like a word.

regulatory.title: EU signals relief over new US tariffs as Trump respects transatlantic truce
regulatory.body: A 10 percent duty will be applied on goods from the EU, respecting a threshold set under the EU-U.S. trade deal last year.

regulatory.title: EU’s Google fine risks triggering Trump as he gears up for more tariffs
regulatory.body: The fine against the U.S. tech giant lands just as Washington prepares new duties that could put last year’s fragile trade truce to the test.

regulatory.title: EU fines Google €890M for breaching Big Tech rulebook
regulatory.body: Brussels orders U.S. search giant to overhaul how it ranks rivals in search results and how it polices its app store — or face further penalties.

regulatory.title: Trump administration steers $5B toward AI research

regulatory.title: Huawei ban to cost the EU up to €40 billion, says industry

regulatory.title: Europe’s 27 leaders to take on AI — finally

regulatory.title: Google mega fine to slash taxpayers’ contributions to Brussels
